newsitem.title: CHINA: China investment in property market down 2.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: China investment in property market down 2.9 pct.

text.p: Investment in China's property sector in the first five months of this year fell 2.9 percent year on year due to state controls and sluggish housing sales, officials said on Wednesday.
"The major reason for the drop was the state's control on investment," said an official with the Real Estate Industry Department of the Ministry of Construction.
China's controls on fixed asset investment had focused on the property sector since 1993, the official said, adding that sluggish sales were another major reaon for the slump in property investment.
By the end of 1996, China had about 66.42 million square metres of vacant commercial space, up nearly 30 percent from the end of 1995, the Market Daily said.
The vacant space had an investment value of more than 60 billion yuan ($7.2 billion), it said.
"The vacant space cause big market pressure on real estate developers," the construction ministry official said.
The Market Daily attributed sluggish sales to high house prices, which were beyond the reach of ordinary Chinese.
Prices for commercial buildings were more than 2,000 yuan per square metre while residential prices were about 1,800 yuan, it said.
